{{Short description|Ethnic identity questions on national censuses}}
[[File:Ethnicity and race in censuses.png|thumb|500px|Map showing countries where the ethnicity or race of people was enumerated in at least one census since 1991 {{Update inline|date=October 2024|map needs updating}}]]

Many [[countries]] and national [[census]]es currently enumerate or have previously enumerated their populations by [[Race (human classification)|race]], [[ethnicity]], [[nationality]], or a combination of these characteristics.<ref name = "pbs">{{cite web|url=https://www.pbs.org/race/000_About/002_03-godeeper.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030426210453/http://www.pbs.org/race/000_About/002_03-godeeper.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 26, 2003 |title=RACE&nbsp;— The Power of an Illusion . Go Deeper |publisher=PBS |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ND1__tXqfDYC&q=%22ann+morning%22+soviet+union&pg=PT11 |title=Ethnicity&nbsp;— Steve Fenton&nbsp;— Google Books |date= 2013-05-02|access-date=2013-06-20|isbn=9780745658438 |last1=Fenton |first1=Steve |publisher=John Wiley & Sons }}</ref> Different countries have different classifications and census options for race and ethnicity/nationality which are not comparable with data from other countries.<ref name = "pbs"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://unstats.un.org/unsd/demographic/sconcerns/popchar/Morning.pdf |title=Approaches To Racial And Ethnic Classification |access-date=2013-03-16}}</ref> In addition, many of the race and ethnicity concepts that appear on national censuses worldwide have their origins in [[Europe]] or in the views of [[Europeans]], rather than in the views of the locals of these countries.<ref name="catdir">{{cite web|title=Census and identity: The Politics of Race, Ethnicity and Language in National Censuses|url=https://catdir.loc.gov/catdir/samples/cam031/2001037352.pdf|publisher=Cambridge University|access-date=2 December 2012|author1=David I. Kertzer |author2=Dominique Arel }}</ref>

{{TOC limit|2}}

==Africa==

===Angola===
[[File:Angola Ethnic map 1970.svg|thumb|right|100px|Ethnic composition of Angola in 1970]]

The [[Portugal|Portuguese]] asked about race in colonial censuses when they controlled Angola, and they provided three options: White, Mestiço, or African/Black. Africans had to then pick either "Assimilado" (assimilated) or "Indigenato" (indigenous).<ref name = "angola">{{cite web|url=https://institutionalizedethnicity.net/country-narratives/angola/ |title=Angola |date=29 July 2011 |publisher=Institutionalized Ethnicity |access-date=2012-09-22}}</ref> Angola has not used any racial categories since its independence in 1975.<ref name = "angola"/> Tribe and language for Africans were recorded only in 1950 and 1960.<ref name = "angola"/>

===Benin===
The people in [[Benin]] were enumerated by ethnicity in 1979, 1992, and 2013 but not in 2002.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Botswana===
[[Botswana]] enumerated people by race in all censuses between 1904 and 1946, and again in the 1964 census (though not in 1956), but in no censuses after 1964.<ref name = "botswana">{{cite web|url=https://institutionalizedethnicity.net/country-narratives/botswana/ |title=Botswana |date=29 July 2011 |publisher=Institutionalized Ethnicity |access-date=2012-09-22}}</ref> People were enumerated by language use in 1946 and 1956 and again in 2001 and 2011.<ref name = "botswana"/>

===Cape Verde===
[[Cape Verde]] enumerated its population by ethnicity in 1950.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Central African Republic===
The [[Central African Republic]] enumerated its population by ethnicity in 1959/1960.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Chad===
[[Chad]] enumerated people by ethnicity in 1993 and 2009.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Democratic Republic of Congo===
The people in the [[Democratic Republic of Congo]] were enumerated by ethnicity from 1955 to 1958.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Republic of Congo===
The people in the [[Republic of Congo]] were enumerated by ethnicity in 1960, 1974, and 1984.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Equatorial Guinea===
The population of [[Equatorial Guinea]] was enumerated by ethnicity in 1950.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Ethiopia===
[[Ethiopia]] enumerated people by ethnicity in 1994 and in 2007.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Gabon===
The population of [[Gabon]] was enumerated by ethnicity in 1960–1961 and 1993.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Ghana===
The population of [[Ghana]] was enumerated by ethnicity in 1960, 2000,<ref name=autogenerated6 /> and 2010.<ref>{{cite web|author=Major Trading Currencies |url=https://www.ghanabusinessnews.com/2012/06/05/group-not-satisfied-with-2010-ghana-census-report/ |title=Group not satisfied with 2010 Ghana census report |date=5 June 2012 |publisher=Ghana Business News |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===Guinea===
The population of [[Guinea]] was enumerated by ethnicity in 1955.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Guinea-Bissau===
The population of [[Guinea-Bissau]] was enumerated by ethnicity in 1950 and in 2009.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Ivory Coast===
[[File:IvoryCoastEthno.jpg|right|thumb|100px|Ethnic composition of the Ivory Coast (Note: the map is in French.)]]
The people of [[Ivory Coast]] were enumerated by ethnicity in 1948, 1957–1958, and 1988.<ref name=autogenerated6 /> The ethnicity data from 1957 to 1958 was only for the [[rural]] areas of the country, though.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Kenya===
Since 1945, [[Kenya]] enumerated people by ethnicity from 1948 all the way up to its most recent census in 2009 (however, the 1999 census ethnicity figures were not made public).<ref name=autogenerated6 /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.minorityrights.org/download.php?id=147|title=Kenya: Minorities, Indigenous Peoples and Ethnic Diversity|author=Maurice Odhiambo Makoloo|type=Report|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080614023538/http://www.minorityrights.org/download.php?id=147|archive-date=June 14, 2008|publisher=Minority Rights Group International}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://kenya.rcbowen.com/people/population.html |title=Kenya - Population Distribution |publisher=Kenya.rcbowen.com |access-date=2012-12-03}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|agency=Associated Press |url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2009/08/25/kenya-holds-first-census_n_268076.html |title=Kenya Holds First Census In A Decade, Causes Outcry Over Ethnic Identity |publisher=Huffingtonpost.com |date= 2009-08-25|access-date=2012-12-03}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.knbs.or.ke/censusethnic.php |title=Welcome to Kenya National Bureau of Statistics |publisher=Knbs.or.ke |access-date=2012-12-03 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130424174848/http://knbs.or.ke/censusethnic.php |archive-date=2013-04-24 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://marsgroupkenya.org/census/?data=ethaf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711040645/http://marsgroupkenya.org/census/?data=ethaf |url-status=usurped |archive-date=July 11, 2011 |title=Kenya 2009 Census Data &#124; Population by Ethnic Affiliation |publisher=Mars Group Kenya |access-date=2012-12-03}}</ref> There were some concerns about asking an ethnicity equation in the 2009 census since it came just a year after the disputed Kenyan presidential election of 2007 and the riots that followed it. Kenya, nevertheless, went through with asking about ethnicity in 2009.<ref>{{cite news|last=Nyambura |first=Helen |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/ozatp-kenya-census-idAFJOE57O0GP20090825 |title=Ethnic question in Kenya census stokes suspicions |work=Reuters |date= 2009-08-25|access-date=2012-12-03}}</ref><ref name="Balaton-Chrimes Cooley p=146879682110563">{{cite journal | last1=Balaton-Chrimes | first1=Samantha | last2=Cooley | first2=Laurence | title=To count or not to count? Insights from Kenya for global debates about enumerating ethnicity in national censuses | journal=Ethnicities | publisher=SAGE Publications | date=3 December 2021 | volume=22 | issue=3 | issn=1468-7968 | page=146879682110563| doi=10.1177/14687968211056379 | s2cid=244893091 | url=https://pure-oai.bham.ac.uk/ws/files/150175243/Kenya_ethnic_enumeration_impasse_accepted_paper_071021_FINAL.pdf }}</ref>

The number of ethnic categories and sub-categories recorded in the country's census has changed significantly over time, expanding from 42 in 1969 to more than 120 in 2019.<ref name="Balaton-Chrimes2020">{{cite journal|last1=Balaton-Chrimes|first1=Samantha|title=Who are Kenya's 42(+) tribes? The census and the political utility of magical uncertainty|journal=Journal of Eastern African Studies|year=2020|volume=15|pages=43–62|issn=1753-1055|doi=10.1080/17531055.2020.1863642|s2cid=231681524|doi-access=free}}</ref>

===Lesotho===
People in [[Lesotho]] were enumerated by race between 1904 and 1976, but not after 1976.<ref name = "lesotho">{{cite web|url=https://institutionalizedethnicity.net/country-narratives/lesotho/ |title=Lesotho |date=29 July 2011 |publisher=Institutionalized Ethnicity |access-date=2012-09-22}}</ref> Language was only recorded in 1946 and 1956, tribe and language for Africans were recorded only in 1950 and 1960.<ref name = "lesotho"/>

===Malawi===
People in [[Malawi]] were enumerated by race between 1911 and 1987, and again in 2018.<ref name = "malawi">{{cite web|url=https://institutionalizedethnicity.net/country-narratives/malawi/ |title=Malawi |date=29 July 2011 |publisher=Institutionalized Ethnicity |access-date=2012-09-22}}</ref> They were enumerated by language only in 1966, 1998, and 2008.<ref name = "malawi"/> They were enumerated by tribal affiliation only in 1926, 1945, and 2008.<ref name = "malawi"/>

===Mali===
[[Mali]] enumerated people in some parts of the country by ethnicity in 1950.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Mauritius===
[[Mauritius]] enumerated its population by ethnicity in 1952, 1962, and 1972.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Morocco===
[[File:Volkeren in Marokko.jpg|thumb|right|100px|Ethnolinguistic composition of Morocco]]
[[Morocco]] enumerated people by ethnicity in 1950 and 1971.<ref name=autogenerated6 /> The 2014 census enumerated people by nationality.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hcp.ma/Note-sur-les-premiers-resultats-du-Recensement-General-de-la-Population-et-de-l-Habitat-2014_a1516.html |title=Note sur les premiers résultats du Recensement Général de la Population et de l'Habitat 2014  |access-date=24 July 2015 |format=docx |work=[[Haut Commissariat au Plan]]}}{{in lang|fr}}</ref>

===Mozambique===
People in [[Mozambique]] were counted by race only in 1894, 1970, 1997, 2007, and 2017.<ref name = "mozambique">{{cite web|url=https://institutionalizedethnicity.net/country-narratives/mozambique/ |title=Mozambique |date=29 July 2011 |publisher=Institutionalized Ethnicity |access-date=2012-09-22}}</ref> The race categories in Mozambique were the same ones as in Angola, due to both being controlled by Portugal before acquiring their independence.<ref name = "mozambique"/> People were counted by language in all censuses since 1940.<ref name = "mozambique"/>

===Namibia===
People in [[Namibia]] were enumerated by race in all 20th century censuses but not in the 2001 census. They were enumerated by language in all censuses since 1951.<ref name = "namibia">{{cite web|url=https://institutionalizedethnicity.net/country-narratives/namibia/ |title=Namibia |date=8 August 2011 |publisher=Institutionalized Ethnicity |access-date=2012-09-22}}</ref>

===Niger===
[[Niger]] enumerated people by ethnicity in 1959/1960 and 2001.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Nigeria===
[[File:Afro asiatic peoples nigeria.png|thumb|right|100px|Ethnic composition of Nigeria]]
[[Nigeria]] enumerated people by ethnicity in 1963.<ref name=autogenerated6 /> In addition, Nigeria has announced plans to enumerate its population by ethnicity in its 2016 census.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.worldbulletin.net/?aType=haber&ArticleID=115785 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130823014011/http://www.worldbulletin.net/?aType=haber&ArticleID=115785 |url-status=usurped |archive-date=August 23, 2013 |title=Nigeria to include religion, ethnicity in 2016 census &#124; Africa |publisher=World Bulletin |date=2013-08-22 |access-date=2013-09-01}}</ref>

===Rwanda===
[[Rwanda]] enumerated people by ethnicity from 1933/34 until 1991.<ref name=autogenerated6 /><ref>{{cite book|first=David E.|last=Kiwuwa|title=Ethnic Politics and Democratic Transition in Rwanda|publisher=Routledge|location=Abingdon|page=71|year=2012|isbn=978-0415616089|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uGclH0p46ogC&q=rwanda%20ethnicity%20census&pg=PA71}}</ref> Due to the [[1994 Rwandan Genocide]] and the ethnic hatred and tensions that caused it, the Rwandan census of 2002 did not enumerate people by ethnicity.<ref>{{cite web|author=Agence France-Presse |url=http://reliefweb.int/report/rwanda/ethnic-origins-ignored-rwandas-first-census-genocide |title=Ethnic origins ignored in Rwanda's first census since genocide &#124; ReliefWeb |publisher=Reliefweb.int |date=2002-08-16 |access-date=2012-12-03}}</ref>

===São Tomé and Príncipe===
[[São Tomé and Príncipe]] enumerated its population by ethnicity in 1950 and 1960.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Senegal===
The people of [[Senegal]] were enumerated by ethnicity in 1960–1961, 1988, and 2002.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Seychelles===
The people of the [[Seychelles]] were enumerated by ethnicity in 1947, 1987, and 1994.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Somalia===
In the pre-independence period in [[Somalia]], the colonial administrations in [[British Somaliland]] and [[Italian Somaliland]] officially classified the [[Somali people|ethnic Somali]] majority within the two territories as "[[Hamitic]]".<ref name="Gbco">{{cite book|title=An Economic Survey of the Colonial Territories, Volumes 1-4|date=1952|publisher=Great Britain, Colonial Office|page=122|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Gr8vAAAAYAAJ|access-date=22 November 2014}}</ref><ref name="Esoa">{{cite book|title=Ethnographic Survey of Africa, Volume 5, Issue 1|date=1969|publisher=International African Institute|pages=45 & 50|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=szhNAQAAIAAJ|access-date=22 November 2014}}</ref> The Italian Somaliland census of 1935 reported that the remaining 6.2% of the area's population consisted of "[[Negroid]] groups", including the [[Somali Bantu|Bantu]] ethnic minorities inhabiting the southern riverine region.<ref name="Kmbeiis">{{cite journal|last1=Menkhaus|first1=Ken|title=Bantu ethnic identities in Somalia|journal=Annales d'Éthiopie|date=2003|volume=XIX|page=323|url=http://www.persee.fr/articleAsPDF/ethio_0066-2127_2003_num_19_1_1051/article_ethio_0066-2127_2003_num_19_1_1051.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131024155331/http://www.persee.fr/articleAsPDF/ethio_0066-2127_2003_num_19_1_1051/article_ethio_0066-2127_2003_num_19_1_1051.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=2013-10-24|access-date=22 November 2014|doi=10.3406/ethio.2003.1051|s2cid=162118204 }}</ref> These census designations were at the time pre-assigned rather than based on self-reporting. Following independence in 1960, no official census was taken until 1975. This first post-independence national census only collected information on district of birth.<ref name="Tmonps">{{cite book|last1=Ministry of National Planning|title=The 1982 labour force survey: analytical report|date=1985|publisher=Ministry of National Planning of Somalia, Central Statistical Department|page=126|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=C5IoAQAAIAAJ|access-date=22 November 2014}}</ref> However, the general government literature maintained that the country's ethnic Somali majority was of Hamitic stock, or alternately of [[Arabs|Arab]] heritage.<ref name="Tmoiang">{{cite book|last1=Ministry of Information and National Guidance|title=Somalia and the Arab League|date=1974|publisher=Ministry of Information and National Guidance|page=7|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4FkMAQAAIAAJ|access-date=22 November 2014}}</ref> Similarly, Article 3 of the [[Constitution of Somalia|Provision Constitution]] adopted in 2012 indicates that Somalia is an Arab nation.<ref name="Fgspc">{{cite web|title=Provisional Constitution|url=http://unpos.unmissions.org/LinkClick.aspx?fileticket=RkJTOSpoMME=|publisher=Federal Government of Somalia|access-date=22 November 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402122013/http://unpos.unmissions.org/LinkClick.aspx?fileticket=RkJTOSpoMME%3D|archive-date=2 April 2015}}</ref> In 2014, the Ministry of Planning and International Cooperation also announced that it would release a new national population census before 2016.<ref name="Sgtlpcaote">{{cite news|title=SOMALIA: Gov't to launch population census ahead of 2016 elections|url=http://koonfurta.com/somalia-govt-to-launch-population-census-ahead-of-2016-elections/|access-date=22 November 2014|agency=Koonfurta|date=10 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141030155132/http://koonfurta.com/somalia-govt-to-launch-population-census-ahead-of-2016-elections/|archive-date=30 October 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===South Africa===
{{See also|Population Registration Act, 1950}}
[[File:South Africa 2011 White population proportion map.svg|right|100px|thumb|Whites as a percentage of the total South African population in 2011]]
[[South Africa]] has enumerated people by race in all of its censuses since 1904.<ref name="southafrica">{{cite web|url=https://institutionalizedethnicity.net/country-narratives/south-africa/ |title=South Africa |publisher=Institutionalized Ethnicity |date=1986-07-23 |access-date=2012-09-22}}</ref> Five population group options are provided in response to the question "How would ''(name)'' describe him/herself in terms of population group?": "Black African", "Coloured", "Indian or Asian", "White" and "Other".<ref>[http://www.statssa.gov.za/census2011/documents/CensusQuestionnaires/Census%202011_q_A.pdf Census 2011 Household Questionnaire A]{{dead link|date=April 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> South Africa has also asked about language use since 1921 for [[white South African]]s and since 1936 for all races.<ref name = "southafrica"/>

===Sudan===
[[Sudan]] enumerated people by ethnicity in 1956.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Swaziland===
The [[Swaziland|Swazi]] census counted people by race in all censuses between 1904 and 1976.<ref name = "swazi">{{cite web|url=https://institutionalizedethnicity.net/country-narratives/swaziland/ |title=Swaziland |date=29 July 2011 |publisher=Institutionalized Ethnicity |access-date=2012-09-22}}</ref> People were counted by ethnic group and tribe only in 1966 and 1976.<ref name = "swazi"/>

===Tanzania===
The [[Tanzania]]n census enumerated people by race from colonial times until 1967, by ethnicity and tribe from colonial times until 1973. It enumerated people by language only in 1952 and 1958.<ref name = "tanzania">{{cite web|url=https://institutionalizedethnicity.net/country-narratives/tanzania |title=Tanzania |date=29 July 2011 |publisher=Institutionalized Ethnicity |access-date=2012-09-22}}</ref>

===Togo===
The people in [[Togo]] were enumerated by ethnicity in 1948, 1958–1960, and 1970.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Tunisia===
[[Tunisia]] enumerated people by ethnicity in 1956.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Uganda===
The people of [[Uganda]] were enumerated by ethnicity from 1948 all the way up to Uganda's most recent census in 2012,<ref name=autogenerated6 /><ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.ubos.org/UgCensus2012/docs/2012_CENSUS_BULLETIN_Vol1.pdf|title=The 2012 Uganda Population and Housing Census|magazine=The 2012 Uganda Population & Housing Census Bulletin|volume=1|date=March 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141113175759/http://www.ubos.org/UgCensus2012/docs/2012_CENSUS_BULLETIN_Vol1.pdf|archive-date=November 13, 2014}}</ref> with the exception of 1980 and possibly 1969.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mongabay.com/reference/country_studies/uganda/SOCIETY.html |title=Uganda - SOCIETY |publisher=Mongabay.com |access-date=2012-12-03}}</ref>

===Zambia===
People in [[Zambia]] were not continuously counted by race before independence, and when they were counted by race it were primarily the non-Africans/non-blacks who were counted.<ref name = "zambia">{{cite web|url=https://institutionalizedethnicity.net/country-narratives/zambia/ |title=Zambia |date=8 August 2011 |publisher=Institutionalized Ethnicity |access-date=2012-09-22}}</ref> People were counted by language only in 1931, while they were counted for ethnicity at various points since 1969.<ref name = "zambia"/> The 1969 census asked about language but not ethnic group, and the 1974 census asked about ethnic group, but not language. The 1980 census asked about ethnic group, mother tongue, and language of most frequent use, while the 1990 census asked about ethnic group and mother tongue. The 2000 census asked about ethnic group, language of most frequent use, and second language.<ref name = "zambia"/>

===Zimbabwe===
People in [[Zimbabwe]] were enumerated by race between 1901 and 2012, but many censuses were done separately for Whites/Europeans and Blacks/Africans before the 1970s.<ref name = "zimbabwe">{{cite web|url=https://institutionalizedethnicity.net/country-narratives/zimbabwe/ |title=Zimbabwe |date=8 August 2011 |publisher=Institutionalized Ethnicity |access-date=2012-09-22}}</ref> People were enumerated by language only in 1982 (when they were enumerated by "[their] father's dialect").<ref name = "zimbabwe"/>

==Asia==

===Abkhazia===
People in [[Abkhazia]] (when it was still a part of the [[Russian Empire]]) were enumerated by [[First language|native tongue]] [[1897 census|in the 1897 Russian Empire Census]].<ref name=autogenerated12>{{cite web|url=https://demoscope.ru/weekly/ssp/rus_lan_97_uezd_eng.php |title=Demoscope Weekly - Annex. Statistical indicators reference |publisher=Demoscope.ru |date=2012-09-16 |access-date=2012-09-21}}</ref><ref name=autogenerated11>{{cite web|url=https://demoscope.ru/weekly/ssp/rus_rel_97.php?reg=0 |title=Демоскоп Weekly - Приложение. Справочник статистических показателей |publisher=Demoscope.ru |access-date=2012-09-21}}</ref> In addition to the Soviet Union enumerating people by ethnicity for its entire existence,<ref name=autogenerated5>{{cite web|url=https://demoscope.ru/weekly/ssp/census_types.php?ct=6 |title=Приложение Демоскопа Weekly |publisher=Demoscope.ru |date=2013-01-15 |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref> the [[International recognition of Abkhazia|partially recognized state]] of [[Abkhazia]] also enumerated people by ethnicity in its post-Soviet censuses of 2003<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pop-stat.mashke.org/abkhazia-ethnic2003.htm |title=Ethnic composition of Abkhazia 2003 |publisher=Pop-stat.mashke.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref> and 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pop-stat.mashke.org/abkhazia-ethnic2011.htm |title=Ethnic composition of Abkhazia 2011 |publisher=Pop-stat.mashke.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===Afghanistan===
Prior to 2010, [[Afghanistan]] had not held a census since 1979 due to the wars and conflicts that have occurred there over those three decades (since the [[Soviet invasion of Afghanistan]] in 1979).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cso.gov.af/Content/files/Population.pdf|title=Afghanistan Statistical Yearbook 2009-10}}</ref>

===Armenia===
People in Armenia (when it was still a part of the [[Russian Empire]]) were enumerated by native tongue [[1897 census|in the 1897 Russian Empire Census]].<ref name=autogenerated12 /><ref name=autogenerated11 /> In addition to the Soviet Union enumerating people by ethnicity for its entire existence,<ref name=autogenerated5 /> [[Armenia]] also enumerated people by ethnicity in its post-Soviet censuses of 2001<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pop-stat.mashke.org/armenia-ethnic2001.htm |title=Ethnic composition of Armenia 2001 |publisher=Pop-stat.mashke.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref> and 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.armstat.am/file/doc/99465273.pdf|title=CENSUS PROGRAMME (CONTENT OF QUESTIONNAIRE) 2011 CENSUS OF THE REPUBLIC OF ARMENIA }}</ref>

===Azerbaijan===
[[File:Azerbaijan ethnic map 2024.png|thumb|right|100px|Ethnic composition of Azerbaijan (2024, after the collapse of the [[List of states with limited recognition|breakaway]] [[Republic of Nagorno-Karabakh]] and the [[flight of Nagorno-Karabakh Armenians]] in 2023)]]
[[File:Azerbaijan ethnic map 1994-2020.png|thumb|right|100px|Ethnic composition of Azerbaijan (1994-2020, after the [[First Nagorno-Karabakh War]] and before the [[Second Nagorno-Karabakh War]])]]
People in Azerbaijan (when it was still a part of the [[Russian Empire]]) were enumerated by native tongue [[1897 census|in the 1897 Russian Empire Census]].<ref name=autogenerated12 /><ref name=autogenerated11 /> In addition to the Soviet Union enumerating people by ethnicity for its entire existence,<ref name=autogenerated5 /> [[Azerbaijan]] also enumerated people by ethnicity in its post-Soviet censuses of 1999<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pop-stat.mashke.org/azerbaijan-ethnic1999.htm |title=Ethnic composition of Azerbaijan 1999 |publisher=Pop-stat.mashke.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref> and 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pop-stat.mashke.org/azerbaijan-ethnic2009.htm |title=Ethnic composition of Azerbaijan 2009 |publisher=Pop-stat.mashke.org |date=1971-04-07 |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===Bahrain===
[[Bahrain]] enumerated people by ethnicity in 1965<ref name=autogenerated6 /> and 2010.<ref name=autogenerated10>{{cite web |url=http://www.census2010.gov.bh/results_en.php |title=Bahraini Census 2010 - تعداد السكــان العام للبحريــن 2010 |publisher=Census2010.gov.bh |access-date=2013-03-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120320104234/http://www.census2010.gov.bh/results_en.php |archive-date=2012-03-20 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The 2010 Bahrain census also enumerated people by their religious beliefs.<ref name=autogenerated10 />

===Bangladesh===
[[British India]] (which Bangladesh was a part of) enumerated its population by race between 1872 and 1941.<ref name="censusindia1">{{cite web|url=http://censusindia.gov.in/Data_Products/Library/Indian_perceptive_link/Census_Terms_link/censusterms.html |title=Census of India - Census Terms |publisher=Censusindia.gov.in |access-date=2013-06-10}}</ref>

===Brunei===
[[Brunei]] enumerated people by ethnicity in all censuses since 1947.<ref name=autogenerated6 /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://unstats.un.org/unsd/demographic/products/dyb/dyb2.htm#2001 |title=United Nations Statistics Division - Demographic and Social Statistics |publisher=Unstats.un.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===Burma===
The people in [[Burma]] (also known as Myanmar) were enumerated by ethnicity in 1931,<ref name=autogenerated27>{{cite web |url=http://www.dvb.no/analysis/burma%E2%80%99s-troublesome-census/21931 |title=Burma's troublesome census &#124; Democratic Voice of Burma |publisher=Dvb.no |date=2009-08-17 |access-date=2013-03-21 |archive-date=2013-01-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130112014144/http://www.dvb.no/analysis/burma%E2%80%99s-troublesome-census/21931 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and 1953.<ref name=autogenerated6 /> A new census which plans to enumerate the people of Burma by ethnicity and race is planned to be held in 2014.<ref name=autogenerated27 /><ref name=autogenerated26>{{cite news|author=Sonu Trivedi |url=https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/op-ed/myanmars-census-a-crucial-democracy-test/article4137474.ece |title=Opinion / Op-Ed : Myanmar's census a crucial democracy test |newspaper=The Hindu |date=2012-11-27 |access-date=2013-03-21 |location=Chennai, India}}</ref> The 1931 Burmese census generated a lot of anger from non-Burmese ethnic groups who were marked as Burmese on the census.<ref name=autogenerated27 /> There is hope that the scheduled [[2014 Burma Census]] will help empower the various ethnic groups in Burma.<ref name=autogenerated26 />

[[The People's Republic of China]] [[Demographics of China|counted people by ethnicity]] since at least [[First National Population Census of the People's Republic of China|1952]] but does not count people by mother tongue.<ref>{{cite news|author=Mark Mackinnon |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/world/asia-pacific/chinas-disappearing-languages-deemed-not-that-important/article1792549/ |title=China's disappearing languages deemed 'not that important' |newspaper=The Globe and Mail |date= 2012-08-23|access-date=2012-09-21 |location=Toronto}}</ref>

People in Georgia (when it was still a part of the [[Russian Empire]]) were enumerated by native tongue [[1897 census|in the 1897 Russian Empire Census]].<ref name=autogenerated12 /><ref name=autogenerated11 /> In addition to the Soviet Union enumerating people by ethnicity for its entire existence,<ref name=autogenerated5 /> [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]] also enumerated people by ethnicity in both post-Soviet censuses in 2002 and 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pop-stat.mashke.org/georgia-ethnic2002.htm |title=Ethnic composition of Georgia 2002 |publisher=Pop-stat.mashke.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===India===
When it was a [[British India|British colony]], India enumerated its population by race between 1872 and 1941.<ref name="censusindia1"/>

In 1872 the first British Indian colonial census classified the population into racial groups through their religion and castes. Later the census also included the categories of tribe and race, although Political Scientist Ram B. Bhagat states that “the distinction between them was often obscure”.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bhagat |first=Ram B. |date=2006 |title=Census and caste enumeration: British legacy and contemporary practice in India |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/29789312 |journal=Genus |volume=62 |issue=2 |pages=119–134 |jstor=29789312 |issn=0016-6987}}</ref> Bhagat also claims that these classes were efforts to try to “identify a race within religion and religion within a race”.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bhagat |first=R. B. |date=2003 |title=Role of Census in Racial and Ethnic Construction: US, British and Indian Censuses |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/4413235 |journal=Economic and Political Weekly |volume=38 |issue=8 |pages=686–691 |jstor=4413235 |issn=0012-9976}}</ref> After the 1872 census, racial categories were only used for the [[Christians|Christian]] population. The five main categories used for this group were Native Indians, [[Asiatics]], non- Asiatics, Mixed Races, and [[Mohammedan|Mohammadian]].  

Drawing from the 1891 British Indian census, the top religious practices were [[Hinduism]] at 72.32% of the population, [[Islam|Islamic]] at 19.96%, and [[Tribal religions in India|tribal]] at 3.23%.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Baines |first1=Jervoise Athelstane |date=1891 |title=Census of India, 1891. General tables for British provinces and feudatory states.: Census Reports - 1891 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/saoa.crl.25318666 |language=English |volume=1|jstor=saoa.crl.25318666 }}</ref> Although these primary religious groups are connected to various races and castes, they created a foundation for enumerating racial groups in India. Writing in 1908, British [[anthropologist]] and [[Physiognomy|physiognomist]] [[Herbert Hope Risley]] stated that “the population of India consisted of seven basic types: [[Mongoloid]], [[Dravidian peoples|Dravidian]], [[Indo-Aryan peoples|Indo-Aryans]], [[Turko-Iranian]], Mongolo-Dravidian, Aryo-Dravidian’ Scytho-Dravidian".<ref>{{Cite book |last=Risby |first=Herbert |url=https://archive.org/details/dli.csl.8916 |title=The People of India |date=1908 |publisher=Thacker, Spink and Co., Calcutta}}</ref> These do not just highlight the classifications for race but also how British India viewed these groups as racially distinctive.

[[File:Indonesia Ethnic Groups Map - EN.svg|thumb|right|100px|Ethnic composition of Indonesia]]
[[Indonesia]] enumerated people by ethnicity in 1930, 2000, and 2010 but not in any other censuses.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UFNKQcvGNSAC&q=census+ethnic&pg=PA20 |title=Ethnic Chinese in Contemporary Indonesia - Leo Heng Chew Suryadinata - Google Books |access-date=2013-03-21|isbn=9789812308351 |last1=Suryadinata |first1=Leo |year=2008 |publisher=Institute of Southeast Asian Studies }}</ref>

People in Kazakhstan (when it was still a part of the [[Russian Empire]]) were enumerated by native tongue [[1897 census|in the 1897 Russian Empire Census]].<ref name=autogenerated12 /><ref name=autogenerated11 /> In addition to the Soviet Union enumerating people by ethnicity for its entire existence,<ref name=autogenerated5 /> [[Kazakhstan]] also enumerated people by ethnicity in its post-Soviet censuses of 1999<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ide.go.jp/English/Publish/Download/Mes/pdf/51_02.pdf|title=Ethnodemographic situation in Kazakhstan|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130120133116/http://www.ide.go.jp/English/Publish/Download/Mes/pdf/51_02.pdf|archive-date=2013-01-20}}</ref> and 2009.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://pop-stat.mashke.org/kazakhstan-ethnic2009reg-census.htm |title=Ethnic composition of Kazakhstan 2009 |publisher=Pop-stat.mashke.org |access-date=2013-03-21 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130622201346/http://pop-stat.mashke.org/kazakhstan-ethnic2009reg-census.htm |archive-date=2013-06-22 }}</ref>

===Kyrgyzstan===
People in Kyrgyzstan (when it was still a part of the [[Russian Empire]]) were enumerated by native tongue [[1897 census|in the 1897 Russian Empire Census]].<ref name=autogenerated12 /><ref name=autogenerated11 /> In addition to the Soviet Union enumerating people by ethnicity for its entire existence,<ref name=autogenerated5 /> [[Kyrgyzstan]] also enumerated people by ethnicity in its post-Soviet censuses of 1999<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stat.kg/stat.files/din.files/census/5010003.pdf|title=5.01.00.03 Национальный состав населения|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090206105009/http://www.stat.kg/stat.files/din.files/census/5010003.pdf|archive-date=February 6, 2009}}</ref> and 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pop-stat.mashke.org/kyrgyzstan-ethnic2009v1.htm |title=Ethnic composition of Kyrgyzstan 2009 |publisher=Pop-stat.mashke.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://pop-stat.mashke.org/kyrgyzstan-ethnic2009v2.htm |title=Ethnic composition of Kyrgyzstan 2009 |publisher=Pop-stat.mashke.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===Russia/Soviet Union===
[[File:Ethnic map of Russia 2010.png|100px|thumb|Dominant ethnicity in each [[Russian oblast]] in 2010]]

The [[Russian Empire]] began counting people by native tongue with [[1897 census|its first modern census in 1897]].<ref name=autogenerated12 /> In 1920, the [[Soviet Union]] replaced this question with a question about ethnicity.<ref>[https://www.un.org/esa/socdev/unpfii/.../workshop_data_stepanov.doc] {{dead link|date=December 2016}}</ref> The Soviet government organized lists of ethnicities and wanted to shape these various ethnic groups in the mold of [[Communism]].<ref name=autogenerated13>"{{lang|ru|Национальный вопрос и национальная култура в Северо-Кавказском крае (Итоги и перспективы): К предстоящему съезду горских народов}}" (''Natsionalny vopros i natsionalnaya kultura v Severo-Kavkazskom kraye (Itogi i perspektivy): K predstoyashchemu syezdu gorskikh narodov''), [[Rostov-on-Don]], 1926.</ref> In the words of Soviet politician [[Anastas Mikoyan]], the Soviet Union was "creating and organising new nations"<ref name=autogenerated13 /> The government of the U.S.S.R. was eager to get ethnic data for many ethnic groups in order to create republics and autonomous regions for many of these ethnic groups and nationalities, and later on (under [[Joseph Stalin]]) in order to deport some of them.<ref name=slezkine>
{{cite journal|author=Slezkine, Yuri|year=1994|jstor=2501300|title=The USSR as a Communal Apartment, or How a Socialist State Promoted Ethnic Particularism|journal=[[Slavic Review]]|volume=53|issue=2|pages=414–452|doi=10.2307/2501300|s2cid=163654746 }}</ref><ref name="martin1998">{{cite journal|author=Martin, Terry|year=1998|title=The Origins of Soviet Ethnic Cleansing|journal=[[The Journal of Modern History]]|volume=70|issue=4|pages=813–861|doi=10.1086/235168|jstor=10.1086/235168|s2cid=32917643 |url=https://dash.harvard.edu/bitstream/handle/1/3229636/Martin%201998.pdf?sequence=2}}</ref> The [[Bolsheviks]] also wanted to get more support from ethnic minority groups within the Soviet Union, many of whom were previously oppressed under [[Russian Tsars|Tsarist]] rule.<ref name="martin1998"/> The Soviet Union continued to ask about ethnicity for the rest of its existence, and [[Russia]] also asked about ethnicity in its two post-Soviet censuses of 2002 and 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://demoscope.ru/weekly/ssp/census_types.php?ct=6 |title=Приложение Демоскопа Weekly |publisher=Demoscope.ru |date=2011-12-26 |access-date=2012-09-08}}</ref> Unlike in 1989, the 2002 census did not require respondents to prove their ethnicity/nationality when they responded to this question.<ref>{{cite web|author=F. Joseph Dresen |url=https://www.wilsoncenter.org/publication/russia-counts-the-2002-russian-census |title=Russia Counts: The 2002 Russian Census |publisher=Wilson Center |date=2002-11-18 |access-date=2013-12-09}}</ref> The number of ethnicity/nationality options available on Soviet censuses was enormous—the Soviet Union offered 194 different choices for ethnicity/nationality in its 1926 census.<ref name=autogenerated4>{{cite web|url=http://www.demoscope.ru/weekly/ssp/rus_nation.php |title=Демоскоп Weekly - Приложение. Справочник статистических показателей |publisher=Demoscope.ru |date=2007-05-27 |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref> There were 97 options in 1939, 126 options in 1959, 122 options in 1970, 123 options in 1979, and 128 options for the Soviet Union in 1989.<ref name=autogenerated4/> There were 192 ethnicity/nationality options for Russia in 2002.<ref name=autogenerated4/>

===Turkey===
Between 1881 and 1893 the [[Ottoman Empire]] implemented its first census, which enumerated the people in the empire by ethnicity.<ref name=autogenerated20>{{harv|Karpat|1978|pp=237–274}}</ref><ref name=autogenerated19>{{harv|Shaw|1978|pp=323–338}}</ref> Some other censuses and studies were conducted in the Ottoman Empire for enumerating the population by ethnicity after the first Ottoman census.<ref name=autogenerated20 /><ref name=autogenerated19 /> After the dissolution of the Ottoman Empire, the first census of the Republic was held in 1927. The last Turkish census to enumerate people based on their native tongue was held in 1965.<ref name="cumhuriyet">{{cite news |url=https://www.cumhuriyet.com.tr/haber/turkiyenin-yuzde-90i-turkce-konusuyor-100768 |work=[[Cumhuriyet]] |title=Türkiye'nin yüzde 90'ı Türkçe konuşuyor |trans-title=90 percent of Turkey speak Turkish |date=21 October 2009}}</ref>

Crampton|via=Google Books |publisher=OUP Oxford |date= 2007|access-date=2012-12-02|isbn=9780191513312}}</ref> Bulgaria directly enumerated people by ethnicity from 1900 all the way up to its most recent census in 2011, with the exception of the 1985 census.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nsi.bg/census2011/PDOCS2/Census2011final_en.pdf|title=2011 POPULATION CENSUS – Main Results}}</ref>

[[Czechoslovakia]] (of which the territory of the Czech Republic was a part) enumerated people by ethnicity in 1921 and 1930, and the Czech Republic did the same thing from 1991 to the present day.<ref name=autogenerated23>{{cite web|url=http://praguemonitor.com/2010/11/30/second-czechoslovak-census-held-80-years-ago |title=Second Czechoslovak census held 80 years ago |publisher=Prague Monitor |date=2010-11-30 |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===Estonia===
People in [[Estonia]] were enumerated by ethnicity/nationality from 1922 to the present day.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www2.ohchr.org/english/bodies/hrc/docs/ngos/LIC_Estonia99.pdf|title=Minority Rights in Estonia|type=Report|publisher= Legal Information Centre for Human Rights}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://pop-stat.mashke.org/estonia-ethnic2000.htm |title=Ethnic composition of Estonia 2000 |publisher=Pop-stat.mashke.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.stat.ee/34278 |title=Population by ethnic nationality, 1 January, years - Statistics Estonia |publisher=Stat.ee |date=2012-03-30 |access-date=2013-03-21 |archive-date=2020-02-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200220181109/https://www.stat.ee/34278 |url-status=dead }}</ref> People in Estonia were also enumerated by native tongue [[1897 census|in the 1897 Russian Empire Census]].<ref name=autogenerated12 /><ref name=autogenerated11 /> During this time period Estonia was under the control of the [[Russian Empire]], then independent, then (excluding [[World War II]]) under the [[Occupation of the Baltic states|Soviet occupation]] and then independent again since 1991.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://estonia.eu/about-estonia/country/population-by-nationality.html |title=Population by Nationality |publisher=Estonia.eu |access-date=2013-03-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120304225022/http://estonia.eu/about-estonia/country/population-by-nationality.html |archive-date=2012-03-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref> There were 192 different ethnicity/nationality options in the 2011 Estonian census.<ref>{{cite web|author=<nowiki>Juhan Tere, BC, Tallinn</nowiki> |url=http://www.baltic-course.com/eng/analytics/?doc=62935 |title=Census 2011: people of 192 ethnic nationalities live in Estonia :: The Baltic Course &#124; Baltic States news & analytics |publisher=The Baltic Course |date=2012-09-17 |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===Finland===
Finland has enumerated its population by language of most frequent use from at least 1990 to the present day.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://pxweb2.stat.fi/Dialog/varval.asp?ma=030_vaerak_tau_102_en&ti=Language+according+to+age+and+gender+by+region+1990+-+2010&path=../Database/StatFin/vrm/vaerak/&lang=1&multilang=en |title=Table: Language according to age and sex by region 1990 - 2011 |publisher=Pxweb2.stat.fi |access-date=2013-03-21 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130106153419/http://pxweb2.stat.fi/Dialog/varval.asp?ma=030_vaerak_tau_102_en&ti=Language+according+to+age+and+gender+by+region+1990+-+2010&path=../Database/StatFin/vrm/vaerak/&lang=1&multilang=en |archive-date=2013-01-06 }}</ref>

===France===
[[France]] has not counted individuals by race or ethnicity since at least 1978, when a law was passed that prevented individuals from being enumerated by these categories without their consent or a state committee waiver.<ref name = "francerace">{{cite web|url=https://docs.google.com/viewer?a=v&q=cache:vLz6pnq_4oAJ:www.brookings.edu/fp/cusf/analysis/laurence.pdf+france+census+race+ethnicity+1872+law&hl=en&gl=us&pid=bl&srcid=ADGEESiJ1dyvouY6Ibx8dja6tnv8e0sqVHvda_pLjbRRf94-Opttxtn4eBTEDpPHnM5A8uyb_RcxB4IVVPWJTc2M_cKtnshQHFZFpIqG53wsjVbhXtoCwZiQaEGMKL3olzpyzvf33sLa&sig=AHIEtbTLE-kOeESgjIHxqg6u_5kmCZk6yQ |title=Powered by Google Docs |access-date=2012-09-21}}</ref><ref name=autogenerated24>{{cite web|last=Bleich |first=Erik |url=http://www.brookings.edu/research/articles/2001/05/france-bleich |title=Race Policy in France &#124; Brookings Institution |publisher=Brookings.edu |date=2001-05-01 |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref> The reasons for this are that many French people consider asking people about race and ethnicity to be a contradiction of their principle of [[Social equality|equality]] and equal treatment for all French people.<ref name=autogenerated5 /> Also, there is a desire to avoid repeating what [[Vichy France]] [[The Holocaust in occupied France|did in regards to its Jewish population]] and to prevent the [[National Front (France)|National Front]] from getting more popularity.<ref name=autogenerated5 /><ref name = "francerace"/> Former [[French President]] [[Nicolas Sarkozy]] and his administration supported and proposed counting French people by race and ethnicity, though this was never implemented.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.civilrights.org/archives/2009/04/255-french-census.html |title=Next Census in France May Track Race, Ethnicity and Religion - The Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights |work=The Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights |publisher=Civilrights.org |access-date=2013-03-21 |archive-date=2012-08-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120817165011/http://www.civilrights.org/archives/2009/04/255-french-census.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Admin |first=The |url=http://blackpoliticsontheweb.com/2012/04/16/despite-ethnic-tensions-counting-voters-by-race-remains-taboo-in-french-presidential-campaign/ |title=Despite ethnic tensions, counting voters by race remains taboo in French presidential campaign |publisher=Black Politics on the Web |date=2012-04-16 |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===Germany===
Nazi Germany enumerated its citizens of Jewish descent in 1939 based on the [[Mischlinge|percent of Jewish ancestry that they had]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wernercohn.com/Paulus.html#5 |title=Bearers of a Common Fate ? The half Jews in Nazi Germany |publisher=Wernercohn.com |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===Hungary===
[[File:Greater austria ethnic.svg|100px|right|thumb|Ethnic composition of the regions of [[Austria-Hungary]] in 1910]]

[[Hungary]] enumerated people by ethnicity in 1880, between 1900 and 1941,<ref>A népesség változó etnikai arculata Magyarország mai területén (map+data+essay) (Kocsis Károly, Bottlik Zsolt, [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] - Földrajztudományi Kutatóintézet, [[Budapest]], 2009, {{ISBN|978-963-9545-19-9}})</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-zZ_NVM9mNEC&q=hungary+census+1941&pg=PA116 |title=Ethnic Geography of the Hungarian Minority on the Carpathian Basin - Kocsis, Károly, Eszter Kocsisné Hodosi - Google Books |date=1938-11-02 |access-date=2013-03-21|isbn=9781931313759 |last1=Kocsis |first1=Karoly |last2=Kocsis-Hodosi |first2=Eszter |publisher=Simon Publications, Incorporated }}</ref> and again from 1980 to the present day<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Ireland===
The 2002 Irish census enumerated people by their place of birth and their country of citizenship.<ref name="autogenerated9">[http://www.irishtimes.com/timeseye/whoweare/p3top.htm ireland.com / In Time's Eye / Who we are] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110304074405/http://www.irishtimes.com/timeseye/whoweare/p3top.htm |date=March 4, 2011 }}</ref> Ireland introduced an ethnicity question to its census in 2006. The 2011 Irish census enumerated people by ethnicity as well, and offered the options White Irish, White Irish Traveller, Other White, Black or Black Irish (with options for African and Other Black), Asian or Asian Irish (with options for Chinese and Other Asian), Other, and Not Stated.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cso.ie/px/pxeirestat/Statire/SelectVarVal/Define.asp?maintable=CD701&PLanguage=0 |title=Population Usually Resident and Present in the State by Age Group, Sex, Ethnic or Cultural Background and CensusYear - StatBank - data and statistics |publisher=Cso.ie |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===Italy===
Censuses in Italy do not inquire about race or ethnicity. Only information disposable are those of civil registers, where only the country of birth is noted down.{{citation needed|date=March 2023}}

===Kosovo===
[[File:Kosovo ethnic 2005.png|thumb|right|100px|Dominant ethnicities in Kosovo in 2005]]

The population of Kosovo was enumerated by ethnicity from 1990s all the way up to the present day.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.icty.org/x/file/About/OTP/War_Demographics/en/milosevic_kosovo_020814.pdf|title=Report on the size and ethnic composition of the population of Kosovo|date=14 August 2002}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://pop-stat.mashke.org/kosovo-ethnic2011.htm |title=Ethnic composition of Kosovo 2011 |publisher=Pop-stat.mashke.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===Latvia===
[[File:Russians in Baltic States (2011).svg|thumb|right|100px|Ethnic Russians as a percentage of the total population in the [[Baltic States]] 2011]]

People in Latvia (when it was still a part of the [[Russian Empire]]) were enumerated by native tongue [[1897 census|in the 1897 Russian Empire Census]].<ref name=autogenerated12 /><ref name=autogenerated11 /> [[Latvia]] enumerated people by ethnicity between 1920 and 1935.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.roots-saknes.lv/Ethnicities/ethnicities_statistics.htm |title=Ethnicities in Latvia. Statistics |publisher=Roots-saknes.lv |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref> During the [[Occupation of the Baltic states|Soviet occupation]] in 1940 and from 1959 to 1989, people were enumerated by the ethnicity.<ref name=autogenerated5 /> [[Latvia]] also enumerated people by ethnicity in its censuses of 2000<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pop-stat.mashke.org/latvia-ethnic2000.htm |title=Ethnic composition of Latvia 2000 |publisher=Pop-stat.mashke.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref> and 2011.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://data.csb.gov.lv/Dialog/varval.asp?ma=TSG11-06a&ti=TSG11-06%2E+RESIDENT+POPULATION+ON+MARCH+1%2C+2011+BY+ETHNICITY%2C+SEX+AND+AGE+GROUP&path=../DATABASEEN/tautassk_11/Final%20results%20of%20the%20Population%20and%20Housing%20Census%202011/&lang=1 |title=Table: TSG11-06. RESIDENT POPULATION ON MARCH 1, 2011 BY ETHNICITY, SEX AND AGE GROUP |publisher=Data.csb.gov.lv |date=2011-03-01 |access-date=2013-03-21 }}{{dead link|date=April 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Lithuania===
People in Lithuania (when it was still a part of the [[Russian Empire]]) were enumerated by native tongue [[1897 census|in the 1897 Russian Empire Census]].<ref name=autogenerated12 /><ref name=autogenerated11 /> [[Lithuania]] enumerated people by ethnicity in its 1923 census and in its 1925 census of its [[Klaipėda]] region.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kasatkina|first1=Natalija|last2=Marcinkevicius|first2=Andrius|title=Russians in Lithuania According to the 1897 and 1923 Censuses: Comparative Analysis|url=http://www.ces.lt/wp-content/uploads/2012/03/EtSt_Kasatkina_Marcinkevicius_2008.pdf|journal=Ethnicity Studies|issn=1822-1041}}</ref> During the [[Occupation of the Baltic states|Soviet occupation]] in 1940 and from 1959 to 1989, people were enumerated by the ethnicity.<ref name=autogenerated5 /> [[Lithuania]] also enumerated people by ethnicity in its censuses of 2001<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pop-stat.mashke.org/lithuania-ethnic2001.htm |title=Ethnic composition of Lithuania 2001 |publisher=Pop-stat.mashke.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref> and 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.15min.lt/en/article/in-lithuania/lithuania-s-population-stands-at-3-043-million-525-259643 |title=Lithuania's population stands below three million |publisher=15min.lt |date=2013-02-04 |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===Luxembourg===
It is illegal to collect statistics about the race, ethnicity, religion or ancestry of Luxembourg citizens.{{citation needed|date=February 2015}}

===Moldova===
[[File:Major ethnics groups in Moldova 1989.jpg|thumb|right|100px|Ethnic composition of Moldova in 1989]]

People in Moldova (when it was still a part of the [[Russian Empire]]) were enumerated by native tongue [[1897 census|in the 1897 Russian Empire Census]].<ref name=autogenerated12 /><ref name=autogenerated11 /> In addition to the Soviet Union enumerating people by ethnicity for its entire existence,<ref name=autogenerated5 /> [[Moldova]] also enumerated people by ethnicity in both its post-Soviet censuses: in [[2004 Moldovan Census|2004]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pop-stat.mashke.org/moldova-ethnic2004.htm |title=Ethnic composition of Moldova 2004 |publisher=Pop-stat.mashke.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref> and [[2014 Moldovan Census|2014]].<ref>[http://www.statistica.md/pageview.php?l=en&idc=479 Results of Population and Housing Census in the Republic of Moldova in 2014]</ref>

===Monaco===
[[Monaco]] enumerated people by ethnicity in 1982.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Montenegro===
[[File:Ethnic map of Montenegro by municipality.svg|thumb|100px|Dominant ethnicities in Montenegro in 2011]]

The population of [[Montenegro]] was enumerated by ethnicity from 1909 up to its most recent census in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.njegos.org/census/index.htm |title=Montenegrin Census' from 1909 to 2003 - Aleksandar Rakovic |publisher=Njegos.org |date=2004-09-23 |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://pop-stat.mashke.org/montenegro-ethnic2003.htm |title=Ethnic composition of Montenegro 2003 |publisher=Pop-stat.mashke.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.transconflict.com/2011/07/montenegro-a-census-like-no-other-147/ |title=Montenegro - a census like no other? |date=15 July 2011 |publisher=TransConflict |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===Netherlands===

In the [[Netherlands]], census data is collected by the [https://www.cbs.nl/en-gb- Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (Statistics Netherlands)], which is distinguished according to country of birth rather than ethnicity or race. Data is collected according to four main categories: Dutch citizen born in the Netherlands with both parents born in the Netherlands, Dutch citizen born in the Netherlands with one parent born in a different country, Dutch citizen born in the Netherlands with both parents born in a different country, or Dutch born in a foreign country.<ref>Statistics Netherlands (2023). How many residents of the Netherlands have a non-Dutch background? [online] Statistics Netherlands. Available at: https://www.cbs.nl/en-gb/dossier/asylum-migration-and-integration/how-many-residents-of-the-netherlands-have-a-non-dutch-background-.</ref>

===North Macedonia===
[[File:Map of the majority ethnic groups of Macedonia by municipality.svg|thumb|right|100px|Ethnic composition of North Macedonia in 2002]]

People in [[North Macedonia]] were enumerated by ethnicity/nationality from at least 1921 all the way up to the present day.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://epc2008.princeton.edu/papers/80013|title=Changes in ethnic structure in Macedonia after emigration of Turkish minority}}</ref> In the most recent census in 2002, 64.2% of the population declared themselves to be [[ethnic Macedonian]]s. The second-largest ethnic group in the country was the ethnic [[Albanians]] with 25.2%. Other major ethnic groups were [[Turkish people|Turks]] (3.9%), [[Romani people|Romani]] (2.7%), and [[Serbs]] (1.8%).<ref name="Statistical Office">[https://www.stat.gov.mk/Publikacii/knigaX.pdf Macedonian census, language and religion]</ref>

===Norway===
Norway enumerated the population in the northern part of the country by ethnicity between 1845 and 1930.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=mbMs68rD9doC&q=norway+census+ethnicity&pg=PA173 |title=Indigenous Peoples and Demography: The Complex Relation Between Identity and ... - Google Books |date=2011-08-15 |access-date=2013-09-01|isbn=9780857450036 |last1=Axelsson |first1=Per |last2=Sköld |first2=Peter |publisher=Berghahn Books }}</ref> In the census of 1970, in limited areas in Northern Norway, people were identified by ethnicity and language.  Such information has not been included in any census since then.<ref>{{cite web| title = Norwegian National Archives | url = https://www.ssb.no/befolkning/artikler-og-publikasjoner/paa-vei-mot-eu-medlemskap | date = 2013
| access-date = 29 July 2014 }}</ref>

===Poland===
People in Poland (when [[Partitions of Poland|the country was still occupied]] by the [[Russian Empire]]) were enumerated allegedly by their native tongue [[1897 census|in the 1897 Russian Empire Census]].<ref name=autogenerated12 /><ref name=autogenerated11 /> Sovereign [[Poland]] enumerated people by ethnicity/nationality in 1921.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kresy.co.uk/census_demographic.html |title=Polish 1921 Census and Demographic Data |publisher=Kresy.co.uk |access-date=2013-03-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130305005728/http://www.kresy.co.uk/census_demographic.html |archive-date=2013-03-05 |url-status=dead }}</ref> It enumerated people by mother tongue in 1931, and used this data to determine ethnicity/nationality.<ref name=autogenerated14>{{cite web |url=http://www6.gencat.net/llengcat/noves/hm04primavera-estiu/docs/moskal.pdf |title=Language minorities in Poland at the moment of accession to the EU, by Marta Moskal |access-date=2013-03-21 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130512204841/http://www6.gencat.net/llengcat/noves/hm04primavera-estiu/docs/moskal.pdf |archive-date=2013-05-12 }}</ref> After [[World War II]], the [[Polish People's Republic|Communist Polish government]] did not enumerate people by nationality/ethnicity.<ref name=autogenerated14 /> The post-Communist 2002 Polish census did enumerate people by nationality/ethnicity and language used at home.<ref name=autogenerated14 />

=== Portugal ===
Census in Portugal do not include a question regarding individuals ethnic or racial background. A question of this kind was recommended to be included for the first time for the 2021 census ("Censos 2021"),<ref>{{Cite web |last=Viegas |first=Nuno |title=Branco, negro, cigano ou asiático? Censos 2021 devem perguntar a etnia, recomenda grupo de trabalho |url=https://observador.pt/2019/04/04/branco-negro-cigano-ou-asiatico-censos-2021-devem-perguntar-a-etnia-recomenda-grupo-de-trabalho/ |access-date=2023-01-26 |website=Observador |language=pt-PT}}</ref> which sparked some controversy. The question was ultimately not included, although a question about religion was included.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Censos 2021: religião sim, etnia não |url=https://ionline.sapo.pt/artigo/734048/censos-2021-religiao-sim-etnia-nao?seccao=Portugal_i |access-date=2023-01-26 |website=ionline | date=9 May 2021 |language=pt}}</ref> A questionnaire regarding ethnicity was planned by the [[Instituto Nacional de Estatística (Portugal)|Instituto Nacional de Estatística]] for late 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=INE avança este ano com pergunta sobre etnia |url=https://expresso.pt/sociedade/2021-04-01-INE-avanca-este-ano-com-pergunta-sobre-etnia-8784b541 |access-date=2023-01-26 |website=Jornal Expresso |date=April 2021 |language=pt-PT}}</ref>

===Romania===
[[File:Romania harta etnica 2011.PNG|100px|thumb|Ethnic map of Romania in 2011]]

[[Romania]] enumerated people by ethnicity in 1859–1860,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.recensamantromania.ro/en/history/censuses-1859-1990/ |title=Censuses of 1859-1990 &#124; Recensamant 2011 |publisher=Recensamantromania.ro |access-date=2013-03-21 |archive-date=2013-05-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130511104834/http://www.recensamantromania.ro/en/history/censuses-1859-1990/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> 1887,<ref>{{cite book | page=407 | title = The Statesman's Year-Book | year = 1889| publisher = St. Martin's Press }}</ref> 1899,<ref>{{cite book | page=612 | title = New International Yearbook | year = 1915| publisher = Dodd, Mead and Company }}</ref> and in every census since 1930, with the exception of the 1948 census, which enumerated people only by mother tongue.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hungarianhistory.com/lib/humis/humis07.htm |title=The Hungarian Minority's Situation in Ceausescu's Romania |publisher=Hungarianhistory.com |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://pop-stat.mashke.org/#romania|title=Population Statistics of Eastern Europe § Romania|publisher=Pop-stat.mashke.org}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.insse.ro/cms/files%5Cstatistici%5Ccomunicate%5Calte%5C2012%5CComunicat%20DATE%20PROVIZORII%20RPL%202011e.pdf |title=Comunicat DATE PROVIZORII RPL 2011_transmis |access-date=2012-12-03 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121114205218/http://www.insse.ro/cms/files/statistici/comunicate/alte/2012/Comunicat%20DATE%20PROVIZORII%20RPL%202011e.pdf |archive-date=2012-11-14 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.recensamantromania.ro/wp-content/uploads/2012/02/Comunicat_DATE_PROVIZORII_RPL_2011.pdf|title=COMUNICAT DE PRESĂ 2 februarie 2012 privind rezultatele provizorii ale Recensământului Populaţiei şi Locuinţelor – 2011|date=February 2, 2012|access-date=November 24, 2012|archive-date=August 2, Jewish Congress]] also carried out a census of [[Romanian Jews|Romania's Jewish population]] in 1947.<ref>{{cite
