===Serbia===
[[File:Census 2002 Serbia, ethnic map (by municipalities).png|thumb|100px|right|Ethnic composition of Serbia in 2002]]

In addition to [[Yugoslavia]] enumerating people by ethnicity/nationality, [[Serbia]] enumerated people by ethnicity/nationality in its 2002 and 2011 censuses.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.osce.org/serbia/30908|title=Ethnic Minorities in Serbia - An overview|date=February 27, 2008|publisher=Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.b92.net/eng/news/society.php?yyyy=2011&mm=11&dd=16&nav_id=77354 |title=Serbia has fewer citizens, census results show |publisher=B92 |date=2011-11-16 |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===Slovakia===
The population of [[Slovakia]] was enumerated by ethnicity/nationality since 1910 all the way up to the present day.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hhrf.org/kisebbsegkutatas/mr_04/cikk.php?id=1188 |title=László Gyurgyik:Hungarians in Czechoslovakia: Changes in Their Population And Settlement System from 1918 to the Present Day |publisher=Hhrf.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://sodb.infostat.sk/sodb/eng/1848-2001/tab.III.2-2B_en.htm |title=Demografickй ъdaje zo sинtania Њudu 1921 |publisher=Sodb.infostat.sk |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://portal.statistics.sk/files/Sekcie/sek_600/Demografia/SODB/Tabulky/Tabulky_AJ_SODB/tab11.pdf|title=Table 11. Resident population by nationality - 2001, 1991|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070715152521/http://portal.statistics.sk/files/Sekcie/sek_600/Demografia/SODB/Tabulky/Tabulky_AJ_SODB/tab11.pdf|archive-date=July 15, 2007|publisher=Statistical Office of the SR|year=2005}}</ref>

===Slovenia===
The population of [[Slovenia]] was enumerated by ethnicity since 1953 all the way up to the present day.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stat.si/popis2002/en/rezultati/rezultati_red.asp?ter=SLO&st=7 |title=Statistični urad RS - Popis 2002 |publisher=Stat.si |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===Transnistria===
People in [[Transnistria]] (when it was still a part of the [[Russian Empire]]) were enumerated by native tongue [[1897 census|in the 1897 Russian Empire Census]].<ref name=autogenerated12 /><ref name=autogenerated11 /> In addition to the Soviet Union enumerating people by ethnicity for its entire existence,<ref name=autogenerated5 /> the de facto independent country of Transnistria also enumerated people by ethnicity in its post-Soviet censuses in 2004 and 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.olvia.idknet.com/ol37-09-05.htm |title=Ol37-09-05 |publisher=Olvia.idknet.com |access-date=2013-03-21 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105231746/http://www.olvia.idknet.com/ol37-09-05.htm |archive-date=2012-11-05 }}</ref> [[Romania]] also enumerated people in Transnistria by ethnicity in its 1941 census.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jewishvirtuallibrary.org/jsource/Holocaust/romanianjewry.html|title=The Plan for the Extermination of Romanian Jewry|work=Jewish Virtual Library}}</ref>

===Ukraine===
[[File:UaFirstNationality2001-English.png|thumb|Ethnic composition of Ukraine in 2001]]

People in Ukraine (when it was still a part of the [[Russian Empire]]) were enumerated by native tongue [[1897 census|in the 1897 Russian Empire Census]].<ref name=autogenerated12 /><ref name=autogenerated11 /> In addition to the Soviet Union enumerating people by ethnicity for its entire existence,<ref name=autogenerated5 /> [[Ukraine]] also enumerated people by ethnicity in its only post-Soviet census in 2001.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pop-stat.mashke.org/ukraine-ethnic2001.htm |title=Ethnic composition of Ukraine 2001 |publisher=Pop-stat.mashke.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===United Kingdom===
In the [[United Kingdom]], the censuses of [[Great Britain]] began [[Classification of ethnicity in the United Kingdom|counting people by ethnicity]] in [[United Kingdom Census 1991|1991]],<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = K. Sillitoe | author2 = P. H. White | title = Ethnic Group and the British Census: the Search for a Question | journal = Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series A | volume = 155 | issue = 1 | pages = 141–163 | year = 1992 | doi=10.2307/2982673| pmid = 12159122 | jstor = 2982673 }}</ref> with [[Northern Ireland]] following in 2001.<ref name="auto">{{Cite journal |last=Cooley |first=Laurence |date=30 August 2021 |title=Census politics in Northern Ireland from the Good Friday Agreement to Brexit: Beyond the 'sectarian headcount'? |journal=The British Journal of Politics and International Relations |volume=23 |issue=3 |pages=451–470 |doi=10.1177/1369148120959045 |s2cid=228856031 |doi-access=free}}</ref> There eventually became more of an interest in enumerating ethnic minorities after large-scale racial minority immigration to the United Kingdom began in the post-[[World War II]] era.<ref>{{cite book|chapter-url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/~uctpb21/Cpapers/Ethn_2gen_revision_C1.pdf|chapter=Ethnicity and Second Generation Immigrants |author1=Christian Dustmann|author2=Tommaso Frattini|author3= Nikolaos Theodoropoulos|doi=10.1093/acprof:osobl/9780199587377.003.0016|title=The Labour Market in Winter: The State of Working Britain|isbn=9780199587377|year=2011}}</ref> The United Kingdom previously planned to enumerate people by ethnicity in 1981, but changed its mind after the large non-response rate to this question in the 1979 Test Census. In 1979, many ethnic minorities refused to answer this question due to the fear of deportation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iser.essex.ac.uk/files/iser_working_papers/2008-26.pdf|title=Who are the UK's minority ethnic groups? Issues of identification and measurement in a longitudinal study|date=September 2008|author1=Jonathan Burton|author2=Alita Nandi |author3=Lucinda Platt |type=Working paper}}</ref> In the [[United Kingdom Census 2011|2011 census]], the ethnic group options for England and Wales were White, Mixed, [[Asian British]], [[Black British]], [[Chinese people|Chinese]] or other ethnic group, and Not stated, with ethnic origin sub-group choices for most of these.<ref name="TIAUKcodes">{{cite web|title=New Ethnicity Code List|url=http://www.theia.org.uk/NR/rdonlyres/9568290B-80AA-4030-AED3-046A8E5C3F92/0/L12V_1_2_NewEthnicityCodes.doc|publisher=The Information Authority|access-date=24 August 2012|archive-date=3 July 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120703112832/http://www.theia.org.uk/NR/rdonlyres/9568290B-80AA-4030-AED3-046A8E5C3F92/0/L12V_1_2_NewEthnicityCodes.doc|url-status=dead}}</ref> The census in the United Kingdom also included a question on country of citizenship between 1851 and 1961.<ref name="catdir"/>

===Vatican City===
[[Vatican City]] enumerated people by ethnicity in 1948.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

==North America==

===Bahamas===
The population of the [[Bahamas]] was enumerated by ethnicity in 1953 and again in 2010.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Barbados===
The population of [[Barbados]] was enumerated by ethnicity in 1946, 1960, 1970, and 1980.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Belize===
Back when [[Belize]] was [[British Honduras]], it enumerated people by ethnicity in 1946. Since gaining independence, Belize has enumerated people by ethnicity from 1980 all the way up to its most recent census in 2010.

===Bermuda===
The people of [[Bermuda]] were enumerated by ethnicity since at least 1950 all the way up to the present day.<ref name=autogenerated6 /><ref>{{cite web|author=Keith Archibald Forbes |url=https://www.bermuda-online.org/population.htm |title=Bermuda's Population and local Expatriate Organizations |publisher=Bermuda-online.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===Canada===
[[File:Canada ethnic origin map 2021.png|150px|thumb|right|A map of the largest ethnic ancestry in different regions of Canada in 2021]]

[[Canada]] [[Demographics of Canada|counted people by ethnic origin]] in 1765 and again from at least 1871 to 2006, with the exception of 1891.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2011/ref/about-apropos/history-histoire-eng.cfm |title=2011 Census - About the census: History of the Census of Canada |publisher=2.statcan.gc.ca |date=2013-01-10 |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref><ref name=autogenerated17>{{cite web|url=https://www23.statcan.gc.ca/imdb-bmdi/pub/instrument/3901_Q2_V3-eng.pdf |title=Archived - PDF Document |publisher=3.statcan.gc.ca |date=2010-05-17 |access-date=2013-01-14}}</ref><ref name="statcan2006">{{cite web|url=https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2006/ref/rp-guides/ethnic-ethnique-eng.cfm |title=2006 Census : Ethnic Origin Reference Guide |publisher=2.statcan.gc.ca |date=2011-05-04 |access-date=2013-03-20}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tRzXJAFODuwC&q=canada+census+1891+ethnic+origin&pg=PA4 |title=Race and Research - Google Books |access-date=2013-03-21|isbn=9780875530307 |last1=Beech |first1=Bettina M. |last2=Goodman |first2=Maurine |year=2004 |publisher=American Public Health Association }}</ref> The options for ethnicity in the 2006 Canadian census were various kinds of [[European Canadian]], [[Aboriginal Canadian]], and various [[non-white]] or non-European groups known officially as "[[visible minorities]]".<ref name=autogenerated17 /> The 2011 Canadian census did not ask about race and ethnicity,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gazette.gc.ca/rp-pr/p1/2010/2010-08-21/html/order-decret-eng.html |title=Archived — Canada Gazette – Orders in Council |publisher=Gazette.gc.ca |date=2012-11-09 |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref> but the new voluntary National Household Survey (NHS) for that year did ask about race and ethnicity (as well as many other questions that were previously asked on the Canadian census).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www12.statcan.gc.ca/NHS-ENM/ref/Questionnaires/2011NHS-ENM-eng.cfm#Q17 |title=2011 National Household Survey Questions |publisher=2.statcan.gc.ca |access-date=2013-03-21 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110809041130/http://www12.statcan.gc.ca/NHS-ENM/ref/Questionnaires/2011NHS-ENM-eng.cfm#Q17 |archive-date=2011-08-09 }}</ref> Prior to the 1981 Canadian census, respondents could only mark one ethnicity/ethnic ancestry, but the 1981 census and all future ones allowed multiple ethnicity responses.<ref name="statcan2006"/> Canada also enumerated its population by place of birth from 1871 to the present day.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.statcan.gc.ca/pub/11-516-x/sectiona/4147436-eng.htm |title=Historical statistics of Canada: Section A: Population and Migration |publisher=Statcan.gc.ca |date=2008-10-22 |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www12.statcan.ca/census-recensement/2006/as-sa/97-557/pdf/97-557-XIE2006001.pdf |title=Microsoft Word - 97-557-XIE_immigration_26-11-07.doc |access-date=2013-03-16 |archive-date=2013-01-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130124085240/http://www12.statcan.ca/census-recensement/2006/as-sa/97-557/pdf/97-557-XIE2006001.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Costa Rica===
[[Costa Rica]] asked a question on ethnic or racial ancestral origins in the 2022 census using multiple options including indigenous, Black or Afro-descendant, Mulatto, Chinese, [[Mestizo]], white and other.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://admin.inec.cr/sites/default/files/media/_por_que_se_hacen_estas_preguntas_1.pdf|title=INEC Cuestionario Censo 2022|website=INEC|date=2022|accessdate= 9 June 2024}}</ref>

Previously Costa Rica enumerated people by ethnicity in 1927 and 1950.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Cuba===
[[Cuba]] enumerated people by race since 1774 to the most recent official census in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://digital.tcl.sc.edu/cdm4/document.php?CISOROOT=/CCC&CISOPTR=1683&REC=5&CISOBOX=foreign|title=Report on the Census of Cuba, 1899 :: Census of Cuba 1899|website=Digital.tcl.sc.edu|access-date=5 March 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.onei.gob.cu/sites/default/files/informe_nacional_censo_0.pdf|title=Censo de poblacion y viviendas Cuba|date=January 2014|access-date=5 March 2020}}</ref>

===Dominica===
The people in [[Dominica]] were enumerated by ethnicity in 1960 and 1981.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Dominican Republic===
The [[2022 Dominican Republic Census]] asked people to choose from "black", "white", "''indio''", "''mulato''", "''mestizo''", "Asian", and "other".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.one.gob.do/media/fdholyvz/boleta-censal-xcnpv.pdf|title=Boleta Censal|website=Nacional de Población y Vivienda|accessdate=17 January 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://acento.com.do/opinion/el-tema-etnico-racial-en-los-censos-nacionales-de-poblacion-de-rd-y-3-9114716.html | title=El tema étnico-racial en los censos nacionales de población de RD (Y 3) |language=Spanish |date=5 October 2022|accessdate=7 September 2024}}</ref>
Previously people in the Dominican Republic had been enumerated by ethnicity in [[1960 Dominican Republic Census|1960]].<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Grenada===
The people of [[Grenada]] were enumerated by ethnicity in 1960 and 1981.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Guatemala===
[[Guatemala]] has enumerated people by ethnicity in 1950, 1964, 2002, and 2018.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Jamaica===
The population of Jamaica was enumerated by ethnicity in 1960 and again from 1982 all the way up to the present day.<ref name=autogenerated6 /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.caricomstats.org/Files/Publications/NCR%20Reports/Jamaica.pdf|title=2000 Round of Population and Housing Census Data Analysis Sub-Project|access-date=2012-12-03|archive-date=2012-01-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120125102835/http://www.caricomstats.org/Files/Publications/NCR%20Reports/Jamaica.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://statinja.gov.jm/PublicationReleases.aspx |access-date=July 19, 2019 |title=Census 2011 General Report}}</ref>

===Mexico===
[[Mexico]] enumerates people on whether or not they speak [[Spanish language|Spanish]] or indigenous languages.<ref name="autogenerated2001">{{Cite web|url=http://sociology.as.nyu.edu/docs/IO/1043/Pop.Comp.IESBS.2001.pdf|title=Population Composition by Race and Ethnicity: North America}}</ref> Mexico does not enumerate its population by race and ethnicity directly.<ref name="autogenerated2001"/>

===Panama===
[[Panama]] has enumerated people by ethnicity from the 1970 census all the way up to its most recent census in 2010.<ref name=autogenerated6 /><ref>{{cite web|author=Don Winner |url=http://www.panama-guide.com/article.php/20100511134852268 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100516050019/http://www.panama-guide.com/article.php/20100511134852268 |url-status=usurped |archive-date=May 16, 2010 |title=National Census in Panama This Sunday, 16 May 2010 |publisher=Panama Guide |access-date=2013-03-16}}</ref> People in the then-United States-controlled [[Panama Canal Zone]] were numerated by ethnicity in 1950 and 1960.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Puerto Rico===
[[Puerto Rico]] enumerated people by race in its census [[Demographics of Puerto Rico|since at least 1877]] with the exception of the period from 1960 to 1990.

===United States===
{{details|Race and ethnicity in the United States Census}}

[[File:Census-2000-Data-Top-US-Ancestries-by-County.svg|400px|thumb|right|The [[wikt:plurality|plurality]] (not [[majority]]) ethnic ancestry in each [[county (United States)|county in the United States of America]]]]

Before the [[American Revolutionary War|U.S. acquired independence from Great Britain]], many of the [[Thirteen Colonies]] conducted [[censuses]] of their own where they enumerated their populations by [[Race (human classification)|race]].<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/08/22/opinion/fix-the-census-archaic-racial-categories.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0 | work=The New York Times | first=Kenneth | last=Prewitt | title=Fix the Census' Archaic Racial Categories | date=2013-08-21}}</ref><ref name="census5">{{cite web|url=https://www2.census.gov/prod2/statcomp/documents/CT1970p2-13.pdf |title=2-11-Z-Colonial & Pre-Federal.pdf |access-date=2013-06-20}}</ref> The [[United States]] as a whole [[Race and ethnicity in the United States Census|enumerated people by race]] in every [[United States Census|census]] since [[U.S. Census, 1790|its first census]] in 1790.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.census.gov/population/www/documentation/twps0056/twps0056.html |title=Historical Census Statistics on Population Totals By Race, 1790 to 1990, and By Hispanic Origin, 1970 to 1990, For The United States, Regions, Divisions, and States |publisher=Census.gov |access-date=2013-05-04 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141224151538/http://www.census.gov/population/www/documentation/twps0056/twps0056.html |archive-date=2014-12-24 }}</ref>  Part of the reason why the United States began counting people by race much sooner than many other countries was due to the [[Three Fifths Compromise]], which determined the amount of representation that Southern states had based on how many slaves they had (slaves were counted as three-fifths of a person for representation purposes, and a new census every ten years was needed to enumerate the current slave population).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.csa.com/discoveryguides/census/review3.php |title=Multiracial Identity and the U.S. Census, ProQuest Discovery Guides |publisher=Csa.com |access-date=2013-03-21 |archive-date=2013-03-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130311012135/http://www.csa.com/discoveryguides/census/review3.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> Initially, the [[United States Census]] only counted Americans as either [[White American|white]] or [[African American|black]], with blacks classified as either [[Free people of color|free]] or [[slaves]] until 1860 ([[slavery in the United States]] was [[Thirteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution|abolished]] in 1865).<ref name="usrace2002">{{cite web |url=https://www.census.gov/population/www/documentation/twps0056/twps0056.html |title=Historical Census Statistics on Population Totals By Race, 1790 to 1990, and By Hispanic Origin, 1970 to 1990, For The United States, Regions, Divisions, and States |publisher=Census.gov |access-date=2012-09-21 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141224151538/http://www.census.gov/population/www/documentation/twps0056/twps0056.html |archive-date=2014-12-24 }}</ref> Over time, the United States has also added some other racial categories as well.<ref name="usrace2002"/> [[Asian-American|Asian]] and [[Indigenous peoples of the Americas|Native American]] categories were added in 1860.<ref name="usrace2002"/> However, the first census to enumerate all Native Americans occurred in 1890.<ref name="usrace2002"/> Before that point Native Americans living on [[Indian reservation|reservations]] were not counted, and thus most Native Americans in the U.S. were not counted in census data before 1890.<ref name="usrace2002"/> Between 1850 and 1870, and in 1890, 1910, and 1920, the [[U.S. Census Bureau]] also enumerated [[Mulattoes]] and sometimes other partially black groups ([[Quadroons]] and [[Octoroons]]) separately.<ref name="usrace2002"/>

The [[U.S. Census Bureau]] counted [[Mexicans]] as a separate race in 1930<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://chnm.gmu.edu/staff/sharon/readings/ngai.html |author=Mae M. Ngai |title= The Architecture of Race in American Immigration Law: A Reexamination of the Immigration Act of 1924|journal= The Journal of American History|volume=86|issue=1|publisher=The History Cooperative |via=Chnm.gmu.edu |access-date=2013-06-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141127115837/http://chnm.gmu.edu/staff/sharon/readings/ngai.html|archive-date=November 27, 2014}}</ref> and tried to retroactively determine the number of Mexicans in the U.S. in 1910 and 1920 as well.<ref name="usrace2002"/>

President [[Franklin D. Roosevelt]] promoted a [[Good Neighbor policy|"good neighbor" policy]] that sought better relations with Mexico.  In 1935, a [[federal judge]] ruled that three Mexican immigrants were ineligible for citizenship because they were not white, as required by federal law<!-- citation need -->.  Mexico protested, and Roosevelt decided to circumvent the decision and make sure the federal government treated Hispanics as white.  The [[U.S. State Department|State Department]], the Census Bureau, the [[U.S. Labor Department|Labor Department]], and other [[government agencies]] therefore made sure to uniformly classify people of Mexican descent as white.  This policy encouraged the [[League of United Latin American Citizens]] in its quest to minimize discrimination by asserting their whiteness.<ref>Patrick D. Lukens, ''A Quiet Victory for Latino Rights: FDR and the Controversy over Whiteness'' (University of Arizona Press, 2012)</ref>

Hispanics were counted as whites in 1940, but for the first time ever, the U.S. made an attempt to measure the size of the Hispanic population that year.<ref name="usrace2002"/> The U.S. resumed enumerating its [[Hispanic]]/Latino population in 1970, with Hispanics being enumerated in every U.S. census since then.<ref name="usrace2002"/> The U.S. Census Bureau also began offering Hispanics several sub-group options from which they could identify themselves, such as Mexican, Puerto Rican, Cuban, et cetera (these Hispanic sub-group options have changed over time).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.census.gov/population/www/documentation/twps0056/tabD-04.pdf |title=Table D-4. Hispanic Origin (of Any Race), for the United States, Regions, Divisions, and States: 1940 and 1970 (Sample Data) (See text for sources, definitions, and explanations) |access-date=2017-12-07 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130120101537/http://www.census.gov/population/www/documentation/twps0056/tabD-04.pdf |archive-date=2013-01-20 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.census.gov/population/www/documentation/twps0056/tabD-02.pdf |title=Table D-2. Hispanic Origin (of Any Race), for the United States, Regions, Divisions, and States: 1990 (Sample Data) (See text for sources, definitions, and explanations) |access-date=2017-12-07 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130120101352/http://www.census.gov/population/www/documentation/twps0056/tabD-02.pdf |archive-date=2013-01-20 }}</ref> The Other race category was added in 1950, and in 2000 multi-race responses were tabulated for the first time  (instructions now explicitly inform respondents that they can choose multiple race boxes).<ref name="usrace2002"/> Because multiracial respondents are now allowed, U.S. Census data since 2000 is not directly comparable with that of previous censuses.<ref name="usrace2002"/> While people nowadays are enumerated by race based on self-identification, until 1950 their race on the census was mainly determined by their census enumerator.<ref name="usrace2002"/> During this time multiracial people who were White and of another race were usually marked down as belonging to the other race due to the [[One drop rule]].<ref name="usrace2002"/> The instructions provided to enumerators endorsed this practice.

It is worth noting that some of the definitions of race in the United States changed over time. For instance, [[Indian Americans]] were previously marked as Hindu in 1920–1940, Other race in 1950–1960, and White in 1970 before being marked as Asian (Indian) since 1980.<ref name = "usrace2002"/> The [[U.S. census]] counted certain [[Asian people|Asian]] ethnic groups separately since 1870, initially counting only [[Chinese Americans|Chinese]] and [[Japanese Americans|Japanese]], but having other categories as well since 1910.<ref name = "usrace2002"/> It only began counting all people by ethnic ancestry since [[U.S. Census, 1980|the 1980 census]], though.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://usa.ipums.org/usa/voliii/items1980.shtml |title=IPUMS USA: 1980 Census Questions and Instructions |publisher=Usa.ipums.org |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref> In addition to a Hispanic/Latino ''ethnicity'' question that has appeared on the census short form since 1980 (based on the US [[Office of Management and Budget]]'s official categories specified in 1977). In addition, at various times the Census Bureau has also used an ''ancestry'' question. Before 1970, [[Alaska]] and [[Hawaii]] had different choices for race on their censuses in contrast to the [[continental United States]].<ref name="usrace2002"/>

The United States has also used language as a way to classify people by race or ethnicity.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Leeman|first=Jennifer|date=2004|title=Racializing language: A history of linguistic ideologies in the US Census|url=https://www.academia.edu/335479|journal=Journal of Language and Politics|language=en|volume=3|issue=3|pages=507–534|issn=1569-2159|doi=10.1075/jlp.3.3.08lee}}</ref> From 1910 to 1940, the Census recorded the mother tongue of the foreign-born population and their children.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.census.gov/population/www/documentation/twps0029/tab06.html |title=Tech Paper 29: Table 6. Mother Tongue of the Foreign-Born Population: 1910 to 1940, 1960, and 1970 |publisher=Census.gov |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref> In 1960 and 1970 the Census Bureau also used mother tongue to classify respondents by ethnicity, but the definition of mother tongue was not consistent. Since 1980, the Census Bureau has tabulated [[Language Spoken at Home|language spoken at home]] for people aged five or older.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.census.gov/hhes/socdemo/language/data/acs/Table2.xls |title=Table 2 (download) |publisher=Census.gov }}</ref>

The [[2020 United States Census]] might allow [[Middle Easterners]] and [[North African American|North Africans]] to write in their ethnicity/race instead of merely marking them as White.<ref name=autogenerated8>{{cite news|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/08/09/census-bureau-changes-race-hispanics-negro_n_1760467.html |title=Census Bureau Proposes Changes: Hispanics As Distinct Category And End Use Of Term 'Negro' |publisher=Huffingtonpost.com |date= 2012-08-09|access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Turnbull |first=Lornet |url=http://seattletimes.com/html/localnews/2019032486_censuschange31m.html |title=Latinos may get own race category on census form &#124; Local News |newspaper=The Seattle Times |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref> Right now, and in the past, [[Arab Americans|Arabs]] have been marked in the U.S. Census as White.<ref name=autogenerated8 /> This began in the early twentieth century when [[Arabs]] [[Immigration to the United States|coming to the United States]] successfully petitioned to be marked as White in order to avoid entry quotas and have a greater chance of achieving success and avoiding discrimination.<ref
name=autogenerated8/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aaiusa.org/pages/not-quite-white-race-classification-and-the-arab-american-experience |title=Not Quite White: Race Classification and the Arab American Experience &#124; The Arab American Institute |publisher=Aaiusa.org |access-date=2013-06-20 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140826035428/http://www.aaiusa.org/pages/not-quite-white-race-classification-and-the-arab-american-experience |archive-date=2014-08-26 }}</ref>

The United States is one of the countries that uses racial and ethnic census data in order to create [[minority-majority districts]], as is required by the 1965 [[Voting Rights Act]].<ref name=autogenerated2>{{cite web|url=http://www.personal.psu.edu/ljk20/MAJ-MINOR.pdf|title=African American Turnout in Majority-Minority Districts|author=Luke Keele|author2=Ismail White|date=December 13, 2011|access-date=December 1, 2012|archive-date=November 7, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141107123620/http://www.personal.psu.edu/ljk20/MAJ-MINOR.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> These districts were created in order to increase minority representation in the [[United States Congress]] following the end of legal [[Racial segregation|segregation]] and racial discrimination in the [[Southern United States]].<ref name=autogenerated2 />

Since 1850, the United States enumerated its population by their country of birth of its population.<ref name=autogenerated21>{{cite web|url=https://www.census.gov/population/www/documentation/twps0081/twps0081.html |title=Historical Census Statistics on the Foreign-Born Population of the United States: 1850-2000 |publisher=Census.gov |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref> The whole U.S. population was enumerated by country of birth between 1850 and 1930 and again from 1960 to the present day.<ref name=autogenerated21 /> Meanwhile, only the [[White Americans|White population of the United States]] was enumerated by their country of birth in 1940 and 1950.<ref name=autogenerated21 />

==Oceania==

===Australia===
Australia enumerated its population by ''race'' between 1911 and 1966, by ''racial origin'' in 1971 and 1976, by ''ethnic'' origin in 1981, and by ''ancestry'' since 1986.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2071.0Feature+Article2July+2011 |title=2071.0 - Reflecting a Nation: Stories from the 2011 Census, July 2011 |publisher=Abs.gov.au |date=2012-06-20 |access-date=2013-04-06}}</ref>

===Fiji===
The population of [[Fiji]] was enumerated by ethnicity from 1881 all the way up to Fiji's most recent census in 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.spc.int/prism/country/fj/stats/Key%20Stats/Population/1.1%20census%20of%20population.pdf|title=1.1 CENSUS OF POPULATION NY ETHNICITY 1881 - 2007|publisher=Fiji Bureau of Statistics |date=June 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121114214328/http://www.spc.int/prism/country/fj/stats/Key%20Stats/Population/1.1%20census%20of%20population.pdf|archive-date=November 14, 2012}}</ref>

===Nauru===
The population of [[Nauru]] was enumerated by ethnicity between 1947 and 1977.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===New Zealand===
[[File:MaoriPopulationPercentage.png|thumb|right|100px|Maoris as a percentage of the total population of New Zealand in 2006]]

[[New Zealand]] enumerated people by ethnicity from 1858 to the present day.<ref name=autogenerated7>{{cite web |url=http://www.stats.govt.nz/Census/about-2006-census/introduction-to-the-census/history-of-the-census-in-nz.aspx |title=Introduction to the Census - Statistics New Zealand |publisher=Stats.govt.nz |date=2006-11-24 |access-date=2013-03-21 |archive-date=2013-02-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130214012652/http://www.stats.govt.nz/Census/about-2006-census/introduction-to-the-census/history-of-the-census-in-nz.aspx |url-status=dead }}</ref> People were enumerated by tribal affiliation in 1901 and again from 1991 to the present day.<ref name=autogenerated7 />

===Palau===
[[Palau]] enumerated people by ethnicity in 1995.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===Papua New Guinea===
[[Papua New Guinea]] only enumerated its population by ethnicity in 1971.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

==South America==

===Argentina===
Argentina enumerated its population by their country of birth from 1869 to the present day.<ref name=autogenerated22>{{cite web|url=http://www.indec.gov.ar/webcenso/aquisecuenta/Aqui12.pdf|title=Tendencias recientes de la Inmigración internacional |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070824231326/http://www.indec.gov.ar/webcenso/aquisecuenta/aqui12.pdf|archive-date=August 24, 2007|date=February 2004 |issn= 0329-7586|publisher=Indec}}</ref>

===Bolivia===
[[File:Pueblos originarios de Bolivia.png|thumb|right|100px|Ethnic composition of Bolivia]]

[[Bolivia]] enumerated people by ethnicity in 1950,<ref name=autogenerated6 /> 2001,<ref>{{cite web |author=CEPAL - Naciones Unidas |url=http://www.eclac.org/cgi-bin/getProd.asp?xml=/publicaciones/xml/3/23263/P23263.xml&xsl=/celade/tpl/p9f.xsl&base=/celade/tpl/top-bottom.xsl |title=CEPAL - Los pueblos indígenas de Bolivia: diagnóstico sociodemográfico a partir del censo del 2001 |publisher=Eclac.org |access-date=2013-03-21 |archive-date=2013-07-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130730033155/http://www.eclac.org/cgi-bin/getProd.asp?xml=%2Fpublicaciones%2Fxml%2F3%2F23263%2FP23263.xml&xsl=%2Fcelade%2Ftpl%2Fp9f.xsl&base=%2Fcelade%2Ftpl%2Ftop-bottom.xsl |url-status=dead }}</ref> and 2012.<ref name=autogenerated6 /><ref name=autogenerated25>{{cite web|url=https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/bolivias-census-omits-mestizo-category-17779349#.ULm6AJtQAak |title=Bolivia's Census Omits 'Mestizo' as Category - ABC News |publisher=Abcnews.go.com |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref> The 2012 census included 40 ethnic group options.<ref name=autogenerated25 /> However, it did not include [[Mestizo]] as an option, which critics of current [[Bolivian President]] [[Evo Morales]] say was because he wants more Bolivians to identify as one of the indigenous groups in order to lend more legitimacy to his indigenous-friendly policies.<ref name=autogenerated25 />

===Brazil===
[[File:Brancos no Brasil.png|thumb|right|100px|Brazilian states according to the percentage of [[Whites]] in 2009]]
The [[Brazil]]ian census [[Race and ethnicity in Brazil|enumerated people by race]] in all censuses since [[1872 Brazilian Census|1872]] with the exception of 1900, 1920, and 1970.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sscnet.ucla.edu/soc/faculty/telles/Paper_AffirmationandAmbiguity.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031001033325/http://www.sscnet.ucla.edu/soc/faculty/telles/Paper_AffirmationandAmbiguity.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 1, 2003 |title=Mapping the ethno-racial composition of the Brazilian population has long been viewed as problematic due principally to the am |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref> The Brazilian census classifies people by race as either white, black, pardo (brown), yellow (Asian), or indigenous.

===Chile===
[[Chile]] enumerated people by ethnicity in 1992.<ref name=autogenerated6 /> The 2017 census included an option to identify as part of [[Indigenous peoples in Chile|one of the country's indigenous groups]].

===Guyana===
[[Guyana]] enumerated people by ethnicity from at least 1946 until at least 2002.<ref name=autogenerated6 /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.statisticsguyana.gov.gy/census.html |title=Bureau of Statistics - Guyana |publisher=Statisticsguyana.gov.gy |access-date=2013-03-21}}</ref>

===Peru===
Peru collected data in the 1940 census. In the [[2017 Peru Census|2017 census]], questions about culture and ancestors were asked in more detail for the first time for the population of 12 years old and above.<ref name="census2017">{{cite report |url=https://www.inei.gob.pe/media/MenuRecursivo/publicaciones_digitales/Est/Lib1539/libro.pdf |title=Perú: Perfil Sociodemográfico |page = 214 |publisher= [[Instituto Nacional de Estadística e Informática]]|access-date=5 March 2020}}</ref> Results were  [[Mestizo]] 60.2%,  [[Quechua people|Quechua]] 22.3%, [[White Peruvians|White]] 5.9%, [[Afro-Peruvians|Afro-descendant]] 3.6%, [[Aymara people|Aymara]] 2.4%, [[Indigenous peoples in Peru|Native or indigenous]] to the [[Amazon basin|Amazon]] 0.3%, [[Asháninka]] 0.2%, Part of another Indigenous 0.2%, [[Aguaruna people|Aguaruna/Awajún]] 0.2%, [[Shipibo-Conibo people|Shipibo-Conibo/Konibo]] 0.1%, [[Japanese Peruvians|Japanese]] ([[Japanese diaspora|Nikkei]]) 0.1%, [[Chinese Peruvians|Chinese]] (Tusan) 0.1%, Other 1.1%.<ref name="census2017"/>
